info.title: Bike4Mind API
info.description:
Programmatic access to the Bike4Mind API. Schemas are generated from the same Zod definitions that validate requests at runtime, so this spec cannot drift from the implementation - with one documented exception: a `pollResult` schema (see the `x-poll-result` extension) describes a handoff response's outcome on a plain, non-contract endpoint, so it is hand-maintained against that handler rather than runtime-validated, and can drift if the handler changes without a matching schema update.

## Getting started
1. Create a key in the web app under **Profile > API Keys** (pick a scope preset).
2. Make a first call: `GET /api/v1/me` with `Authorization: Bearer b4m_live_<key>`. It needs only the `me:read` scope, spends no credits, and returns your identity, plan tier and credit balance.
3. Read the rest of this page for the behaviour shared across endpoints: rate limits, credits, errors and async jobs.

Endpoints are grouped by tag: **AI** (chat, completions, embeddings, agent runs, tools, quest polling), **Images**, **Audio**, **Videos**, **Music**, **Transcriptions**, **Sessions**, **Artifacts**, **Files**, **Projects**, **Agents**, **Data Lakes**, **Data Lake Research**, **Skills**, **Functions** and **Account**.

## Authentication
Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer b4m_live_<key>` (canonical), `x-api-key: b4m_live_<key>` (legacy), or `Authorization: ApiKey b4m_live_<key>`. A JWT access token is also accepted in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

## Scopes
API keys carry `resource:action` scopes. The documented scopes are:
- `notebooks:read`
- `notebooks:write`
- `files:read`
- `files:write`
- `ai:generate`
- `ai:decide`
- `ai:chat`
- `projects:read`
- `projects:write`
- `agents:read`
- `agents:write`
- `me:read`
- `personas:mint`
- `marketing-reports:read`
- `marketing-reports:write`
- `hearth:read`
- `hearth:write`
- `datalake:read`
- `datalake:write`
- `datalake:share`
- `datalake:query`
- `overwatch:read`
- `skills:read`
- `skills:write`
- `skills:review`
- `bob:read`
- `bob:run`
- `slack:post`
- `api-keys:manage`
- `ai:end-user-id`
- `artifacts:publish`
- `functions:invoke`
- `functions:author`

Per-operation required scopes are published via the `x-required-scopes` extension. Semantics are OR: a key needs ANY ONE of an operation's listed scopes, not all of them. Operations with no `x-required-scopes` enforce no scope (e.g. the JWT-only tools endpoint).

## Rate limits
Each API key has a per-minute and a per-day request ceiling, by default 60 requests/minute and 1000 requests/day (a key can be minted with its own ceilings). Responses from rate-limited operations carry the current state of both windows (the streaming completions endpoint sends them only on an API-key `429`):
- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Minute`
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Minute`
- `X-RateLimit-Reset-Minute`
- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Day`
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Day`
- `X-RateLimit-Reset-Day`

Reset values are Unix epoch seconds. Exceeding a ceiling returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header; wait that long before retrying. This includes `POST /api/ai/v1/completions`, which rate-limits before it opens its event stream. `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/credits`, `GET /api/v1/models`, `GET /api/v1/image-models`, `GET /api/v1/video-models`, `GET /api/v1/music-models`, the `GET` list endpoints for `/api/v1/sessions`, `/api/v1/video-generations`, `/api/v1/music-generations` and `/api/v1/image-jobs`, and the poll endpoints listed under Async jobs are exempt from the per-day ceiling: a poll consumes no daily slot, and only the per-minute limit applies. A request refused at the route scope gate (`403`) or for a bad key (`401`) never reaches the limiter and carries no rate-limit headers.

## Credits
Generation endpoints spend credits from the balance shown at `credits.balance` on `GET /api/v1/me` (the caller's personal ledger). A key without `me:read` reads the same number from `GET /api/v1/credits`, which accepts `ai:chat`, `ai:generate` and `ai:decide` too. A synchronous call that cannot be paid for fails with `422` and `errorCode: "insufficient_credits"`. On a queued job the same code arrives on the polled result instead (see Async jobs), so check both places.

## Errors
Error bodies use one envelope, the `ErrorResponse` schema: `{ "error": string, "request_id"?: string }`, plus an `errorCode` on failures a client is expected to branch on (`insufficient_credits`, `spend_cap_exceeded`, `provider_not_configured`, ...). A deprecated `name` field may also appear until its sunset date; do not rely on it. Branch on the HTTP status and `errorCode`, never on the `error` prose. A few operations declare a bespoke error shape for a specific status (e.g. the `500` of the tools endpoint and the `413` of text-to-speech); each operation lists the statuses it can return and the body for each.

The shared statuses: a malformed JSON body is `400`, a body that fails schema validation is `422`, a missing or invalid credential is `401`, a valid key without the required scope is `403`, an unknown resource is `404` and an exceeded rate limit is `429`. A `401` carrying `errorCode: "provider_rejected"` means the upstream provider refused the provider key the request used - the platform key by default, or your own stored provider key when you configured one - so your API key itself was accepted.

## Async jobs
Work that is not provably fast is queued and polled rather than held open:
- **Chat** (`POST /api/chat`) and the deprecated quest-based image routes (`POST /api/v1/image-generations`, `POST /api/v1/image-edits`) return a quest. Poll `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` until `status` is `done` or `stopped`; chat text arrives in `reply`, generated images in `images`, edited images in `files[].url`. Check for failure before reading results: a job that ends `done` with `type: "error"` failed (the reason is in `reply`), and a job that ends `stopped` also failed even when `type` is not `"error"` (its `reply` carries an explanation, not an answer). The outcome schema of each of these quest handoffs is linked from its response via the `x-poll-result` extension. Chat also accepts `wait: true` to block until the reply is ready.
- **Agent runs** (`POST /api/v1/agent-executions`) return `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/agent-executions/{id}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed` or `aborted`.
- **Image generation and editing** (`POST /api/v1/image-jobs`) returns `202` with one job per image. Poll `GET /api/v1/image-jobs/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`.
- **Video generation** (`POST /api/v1/video-generations`) returns `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/video-generations/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`.
- **Music generation** (`POST /api/v1/music-generations`) returns `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/music-generations/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`.
- **Scene composition** (`POST /api/v1/scene-compositions`) returns `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/scene-compositions/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`.
- **Briefs** (`POST /api/v1/briefs`) return `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/briefs/{id}` until `status` is `ready` or `failed`.
- **Follow-up briefs** (`POST /api/v1/briefs/follow-ups`) return `202` too and are polled the same way, at `GET /api/v1/briefs/{id}`.
- **Brief replies** (`POST /api/v1/briefs/{id}/decisions/{decisionId}/reply`) return `202` with the `executionId` of the agent run your reply started. Poll `GET /api/v1/agent-executions/{id}` with it.
- **Research runs** (`POST /api/v1/data-lakes/{id}/research/runs`) return `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/data-lakes/{id}/research/runs/{run_id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.
- **Delegations** (`POST /api/v1/delegations`) return `202`. Poll `GET /api/v1/delegations/{id}` until `status` is `handled`, `needs_decision` or `failed`.
- **Function calls** (`POST /api/v1/functions/{id}/invoke` with `mode: "async"`) return `202` with a `call_id`. Poll `GET /api/v1/functions/calls/{call_id}` until `status` is `finished`, then check `outcome` before reading `output`. Results are kept 24 hours. `POST /api/v1/functions/calls/{call_id}/cancel` cancels a call still `queued` or `running`.
- **File uploads** (`POST /api/v1/files`) return a presigned `upload_url`; after the `PUT`, poll `GET /api/v1/files/{id}` until `moderation_status` is `clean` before passing the id elsewhere.
- **Audio** endpoints are synchronous and return the result directly. A text-to-speech (`POST /api/ai/tts`) or sound-effect (`POST /api/ai/sound-effects`) clip that outlasts the request answers `202` with its job resource instead; it cannot be polled yet, and unless `preview` was set the clip is saved to the file browser when it finishes.
- **Transcriptions** (`POST /api/v1/transcriptions`) are synchronous too: after the upload, one call returns the text. Long audio can outlast the request timeout and fail with a `504`; see that endpoint for the limit.

Poll with a backoff of a few seconds: each poll counts against the per-minute limit.

## Versioning
New endpoints live under `/api/v1`. Published endpoints are forward-only: a live URL is never renamed or removed, and a breaking change ships as a new path while the old one keeps working. Nothing published is removed silently - a deprecated field or endpoint is marked `deprecated` in this spec with a sunset date in its description, and keeps working until that date.

## CORS
The spec (`/api/v1/openapi.json`) is served publicly with permissive CORS. The API endpoints themselves are called server-to-server with a secret key and are not intended for browser CORS use.

## Correlation
Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header (echoed as `request_id`/`requestId` in bodies and events) for log correlation.

bearerAuth.description: Canonical auth. Send `Authorization: Bearer b4m_live_<key>`. A JWT access token is also accepted in this header; a token beginning with `b4m_` is treated as an API key, anything else as a JWT.

apiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
apiKeyAuth.description: Legacy auth. Send `x-api-key: b4m_live_<key>`. Equivalent to `bearerAuth` for API keys.

jwtAuth.description: JWT access token only. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. API keys are NOT accepted here.

request_id.description: Correlation id, mirrors the X-Request-ID header.

name.description: Deprecated, sunset 2026-12-01. The `name` of whatever the server threw - usually one of our own error classes (`NotFoundError`, `UnprocessableEntityError`, ...), but on an unhandled 500 it can be a library or driver class name instead. Unstable by nature: these are internal names we rename at will, and the set is open. Documented only so the wire and this spec agree for the deprecation window; it is removed on the sunset date. Branch on the HTTP status, not on this.

sendChatMessage200PollResult.description: Outcome fields of the quest polled at `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` after this ACK. A finished turn that failed is `status: "done"` with `type: "error"` and the failure text in `reply`, so a caller reading `reply` alone cannot tell a failure from an answer - check `type` first, and also treat a terminal `status: "stopped"` (a missing session, a user-cancelled turn) as failure even though it never sets `type`. `errorCode` is an optional refinement of `type: "error"`, present only for a classified failure; credit exhaustion arrives here as `insufficient_credits`, the same vocabulary the synchronous 422s on `/api/ai/music`, `/api/ai/sound-effects` and `/api/ai/tts` use, and a spending pause that lands after the ACK arrives as `spend_frozen`. A quest that settled before the in-chat QuestMaster plan was retired can still carry `free_quest_limit_reached`; no current turn raises it. `QUEST_ERROR_CODES` also publishes `spend_cap_exceeded`, but no current throw site on this endpoint raises it as a quest errorCode: its only one, the embed chat route's pre-flight 422, fires outside the process try/catch that would classify it onto the quest; `run_budget_exhausted` is raised only by image generation. A turn that prompt moderation refuses arrives as `content_blocked`; do not resend it unchanged. Most `type: "error"` turns - an abort, a provider timeout or overload - have NO `errorCode`; its absence does not mean success, only that the failure is unclassified. A recovered stuck quest that still has renderable content is not a failure at all: it keeps `type: "message"` even though it did not finish, so a caller gets the content rather than an error. `fallbackInfo` is present only when the requested model failed and another model produced the reply: `fallbackModel` answered, `primaryModel` is what was asked for, and `reason` is the error from the first failed attempt on the requested model. The poll body carries further fields not modelled here, including `images`, `files`, `toolPayloads`, `promptMeta`, and the attachment report (`attachmentNotices`/`attachmentDelivery`) - only the outcome subset is modelled here.

example.reply: You're out of credits. This request needs about 12 credits, but only 3 are available.

generateImage200PollResult.description: The quest polled at `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` after this ACK. The render is finished once `status` is `"done"`: on success `images` holds the rendered images; a render that FAILED is `type: "error"` with the reason in `reply`, never a 4xx. That covers credit exhaustion (tagged `errorCode: "insufficient_credits"`, the same vocabulary as the synchronous 422s on the audio endpoints), a provider error, a reference image that is missing, not an image, or still in moderation, and the combined FLUX.2 or FLUX 3 input-image limit after attachments are resolved. Check `type` before reading `images`; `errorCode` is absent on unclassified failures, so its absence does not mean success.

editImage200PollResult.description: The quest polled at `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` after this ACK. The render is finished once `status` is `"done"`: on success `images` holds the rendered images; a render that FAILED is `type: "error"` with the reason in `reply`, never a 4xx. That covers credit exhaustion (tagged `errorCode: "insufficient_credits"`, the same vocabulary as the synchronous 422s on the audio endpoints), a provider error, a reference image that is missing, not an image, or still in moderation, and the combined FLUX.2 or FLUX 3 input-image limit after attachments are resolved. Check `type` before reading `images`; `errorCode` is absent on unclassified failures, so its absence does not mean success.

status.description: `queued` and `running` carry nothing else; poll again. `finished` carries how the call ended.

outcome.description: How a finished call ended: `ok` carries `output`; any other outcome carries `error`. `cancelled` means its caller cancelled it, and nothing it returned is kept.

code_hash.description: sha256 hex of the pinned code.

input_hash.description: sha256 hex of the canonical JSON of the validated inputs.

data.description: Each data file the call read, by hash. Empty while functions read no data files.

uses.description: Other functions the call used. Always empty today.

stamp.description: What the call ran on: the code, inputs, runtime, and packages, by hash and version.

path.description: The field, as a dotted path from the inputs, such as `span`.

invokeFunction202PollResult.description: Read at `GET /api/v1/functions/calls/{call_id}`. A call that ran and failed still polls as `200` with `status: "finished"`; check `outcome` before reading `output`.

tools.description: Explicit tool ids to offer the model. A non-empty array enables tools on its own; no companion `toolMode` or `enableTools` is required. Merged with the auto-selected set under `toolMode: "smart"`, and ignored under `toolMode: "fast"`. This list ADDS to what is offered rather than restricting it - the server still offers tools of its own (for example knowledge retrieval when the session has reachable documents). Unrecognized ids are dropped rather than rejecting the request; the response reports the surviving set as `tools.effectiveTools` and the ids that are not tools in this deployment as `tools.unrecognizedTools`, since no endpoint enumerates the valid ids. `unrecognizedTools` is reported under every `toolMode` - it describes the ids, not what the mode did with them - so under `toolMode: "fast"` an id can be absent from `effectiveTools` (the mode discarded it) without being unrecognized. Both reported lists are deduplicated, and `unrecognizedTools` names at most the first 10 distinct ids.

enableQuestMaster.description: Deprecated and ignored. The in-chat QuestMaster plan this used to start has been retired.

skip_auto_offers.description: Suppress tools the server would otherwise attach on its own for this session (the knowledge-base search offer, in-app view navigation, blog drafting/editing/publishing, skill invocation, and every tool from a connected MCP server). Native tools you request explicitly in `tools` are unaffected, but an MCP server tool cannot be named through this field, so with this flag set a caller with an MCP server connected sees none of its tools regardless of `tools`. One system-prompt block goes with them: withholding in-app view navigation also drops the view-registry block that exists only to describe it. No other prompt content changes. This does not switch off retrieval: a session with forced knowledge retrieval still retrieves, and documents already attached to the session are still placed in the prompt directly. Any promptMode suppresses these too, so false has no effect alongside one.

systemPrompt.description: System-prompt text for this request only, never persisted. Rendered as a defended block appended after every other system-prompt source, with prose instructing the model to defer to organization, session and data-lake guidance. Over the cap is a 422, never truncated.

organization_id.description: The organization whose credit pool pays for this run. You must belong to it; a non-member gets 404. Omit it to bill your personal credits. An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization: omit this or set it to the key's; any other value is a 403 (`errorCode: billing_organization_mismatch`).

confidence_overrides.description: Admin only. Scripted per-iteration confidence scores (0 to 1) that replace the real score at the confidence gate: entry i scores iteration i + 1, and iterations past the end use the real score. The gate pauses the run for review on a streak of consecutive evaluated iterations below its threshold (currently 2), so script one low entry per iteration you want in the streak. Only iterations that ran tools are evaluated, scripted or not, and a finished run never pauses. A non-admin caller gets 403.

example.message: Audit this data set and summarize what stands out.

step_progress.description: Progress through a known number of steps, for a determinate progress display. `completed` and `total` count the same steps, which are not ReAct iterations, so do not pair `total` with `total_iterations`. The whole object is null when the executor cannot predict a total for this run, which is the common case: show indeterminate progress then. A run that has finished its last step can still be `running` while it writes its answer, so treat `status` as the source of truth for whether it is done.

lastUsedModel.description: Pin a specific model id, or omit/send null to leave the current pin unchanged. Sending null does NOT clear it.

lakeScope.description: The data lakes this session searches, as lake tags (the `datalake_tag` of each lake from GET /api/v1/data-lakes). Send a list to search only those lakes, `[]` to search no lake at all, or `null` to clear the choice so retrieval falls back to every lake you can reach. Omit to leave the current choice unchanged. Tags naming a lake you cannot reach are ignored at retrieval time rather than rejected here. A non-empty list also turns forced retrieval on for a session that has never set it, unless `forceKnowledgeRetrieval` is sent in the same request; a value the session already stores is left as it is. Conversely `[]` leaves a session with forced retrieval nothing to retrieve from, so its forced retrieval is skipped rather than run against every lake.

includeLibraryFiles.description: Whether the session grounds on your own library (files you own, or that are shared with you or your groups) alongside its lakes. `false` confines retrieval to lake content, including when every lake is in scope; the session's attached files still reach the model and stay searchable by its knowledge-base tools. Omit to leave it unchanged; while never set, the library is excluded only when a lake was picked for the session (Data Lakes mode or an explicit lake scope), not when lake tags were derived from an attached file. While `forceKnowledgeRetrieval` is `false` the library is included regardless; the stored value applies again once it is turned back on.

promptCacheTtl.description: How long the prompt cache of this chat lives between messages: `5m` (the default) or `1h`. A 1-hour cache costs more to write and the same to read; it applies only on models that support it, and other models keep the 5-minute cache. Omit to leave it unchanged.

propagateToProjects.description: Defaults to true when omitted. When knowledgeIds grows, the newly-added file ids are also appended to every project that contains this session, granting every member of that project access to those files. This propagation is append-only and cannot be undone through the UI - pass false if newly-attached files should not be shared with the project.

newLastNotebookId.description: The caller's most recently updated remaining session, which the product UI opens next; null when none remains.

content.description: A string, or an array of content blocks. Known block types (text, image, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, thinking and the provider blocks echoed back) are validated; a block of any other `type` is forwarded to the provider unchanged. A `system` message may instead hold only `tool_addition` / `tool_removal` blocks (`{ type, tool: { type: "tool_reference", name } }`) to load or unload a tool named in `tools` mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. It must follow a user turn or an assistant turn ending in a tool search result, and be the last message or precede an assistant turn. Only on models whose `supports_tool_changes` is true and that are served by the direct Anthropic API; otherwise refused with `errorCode: "tool_changes_unsupported"` (or `invalid_tool_change` / `unknown_tool_reference` when malformed). A final non-blank assistant turn is an assistant prefill, except a server-tool continuation ending in `server_tool_use` or `tool_search_tool_result`. Plain system prompts and blank messages are ignored. It is accepted only when the selected model has `supports_assistant_prefill: true`; otherwise the request returns `400` with `errorCode: "assistant_prefill_unsupported"` without changing the message.

defer_loading.description: Keep this definition out of the model context until the tool search server tool (or a `tool_reference`) loads it. Honoured only on Claude models (direct Anthropic or Bedrock) whose `supports_tool_search` is true; on every other model it is ignored and the tool is sent as usual. At least one tool, or a `serverTool` entry, must stay non-deferred (`errorCode: "all_tools_deferred"`).

cache_control.description: Accepted for validation only and not forwarded. Rejected on a deferred tool (`errorCode: "deferred_tool_cache_control"`).

serverTool.description: A provider-run tool, sent to the provider as `{ type, name }`. Only the Anthropic tool search tools exist today, and only on Claude models (direct Anthropic or Bedrock) whose `supports_tool_search` is true; any other model is refused with `errorCode: "tool_search_unsupported"` rather than run without it.

run.description: Groups this request's spend under a run you created with `POST /api/v1/completion-runs`. A run you did not create is refused with `404` (`errorCode: "run_not_found"`), as is a read of its spend.

end_user_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the end user this request is for (1-64 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `:`, `-`; never an email). A malformed value is refused with a 400 (`errorCode: "invalid_end_user_id"`). Accepted only on an API key holding `ai:end-user-id`, which an administrator grants to keys that serve many end users; any other credential sending it is refused with a 400 (`errorCode: "end_user_id_not_allowed"`). On models served directly by OpenAI or Anthropic, the provider then receives an identifier derived from your account and this value instead of one for your whole account; other providers receive no end-user identifier.

organization_id.description: Organization whose credit pool pays for this call, or null for personal credits. Omitted: personal credits for a signed-in user. With `run`, send the `organization_id` the run was minted with. An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization, and naming any other (null included) gets a 403 (`errorCode: "billing_organization_mismatch"`). A caller who cannot use the named organization gets a 403.

defer_loading.description: Keep this definition out of the model context until the tool search server tool (or a `tool_reference`) loads it. Honoured only on Claude models (direct Anthropic or Bedrock) whose `supports_tool_search` is true; on every other model it is ignored and the tool is sent as usual. At least one tool, or a `serverTool` entry, must stay non-deferred (`errorCode: "all_tools_deferred"`).

cache_control.description: Accepted for validation only and not forwarded. Rejected on a deferred tool (`errorCode: "deferred_tool_cache_control"`).

serverTool.description: A provider-run tool, sent to the provider as `{ type, name }`. Only the Anthropic tool search tools exist today, and only on Claude models (direct Anthropic or Bedrock) whose `supports_tool_search` is true; any other model is refused with `errorCode: "tool_search_unsupported"` rather than run without it.

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort hint. Honoured by the OpenAI (reasoning models only, and not alongside tools on some of them), Kimi (K3 only), DeepSeek and Anthropic Claude (direct and Bedrock) adapters; each maps it onto its own scale. On Claude, `none` turns thinking off where the model allows it (otherwise it runs at the lowest effort), so short `max_tokens` replies stream visible text from the start; `minimal` maps to `low`. When `thinking.enabled` is also set on a Claude model, thinking stays on and this sets its effort instead, with `none` and `minimal` mapping to `low`. Claude models that reason inside `max_tokens` never have that ceiling raised, and on older Claude models any level above `none` turns thinking on (it is off by default there), forces temperature to 1 and drops top_p, and a thinking budget that cannot fit under `max_tokens` is skipped. On the direct Anthropic API, a json_schema `response_format` with no tools is served by a forced tool on models that support forced tool use, and that tool cannot run alongside thinking. When this field names a level above `none` for a model with adaptive thinking, the schema is served by native structured outputs instead and the level is honoured; thinking then counts against `max_tokens`, which is not raised. A schema that native structured outputs cannot express (for example one that declares `additionalProperties` other than false), or a request whose documents ask for citations, keeps the forced tool and only `none` is honoured. Older Claude models that think with a budget keep the forced tool, so there only `none` is honoured; models served by native structured outputs honour every level. Silently ignored by every other adapter (Gemini, xAI, Ollama) and by non-reasoning models, so sending it there is a no-op.

thinking.description: Ask a model that can think to think on this turn. On Claude, `reasoningEffort` then sets how much it thinks, and `budget_tokens` (default 16000, minimum 1024, maximum 32000) sizes thinking on older Claude models. Ignored by models that cannot think. With a json_schema `response_format` on the direct Anthropic API, a model with adaptive thinking serves the schema through native structured outputs so thinking can run, within `max_tokens`, unless the schema or a citations document keeps it on the forced tool; older Claude models that think with a budget serve it through a forced tool, which cannot run alongside thinking, and ignore this.

cacheTtl.description: Prompt-cache lifetime for this request, where the server places cache breakpoints (Claude on the direct Anthropic API or Bedrock, on requests the server caches: CLI and Desktop always, other callers once the conversation has a prior assistant turn). `5m` (the default) writes at 1.25x the input rate; `1h` writes at 2x and keeps the cached prefix for an hour between requests. Reads cost the same either way. Models without 1-hour caching ignore `1h` and keep `5m`. Every breakpoint in a request must share one TTL: with `1h`, set no `cache_control` of your own unless it also carries `ttl: "1h"`.

organization_id.description: The organization to bill: one you belong to, or null for your personal credits. Omitted bills your home organization, or your personal credits if you have none. An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization: omit this or set it to the key's organization; any other value, null included, is rejected with a 403 (`errorCode: billing_organization_mismatch`).

role.description: `root` for the session that started the run, `worker` for one it spawned.

purpose.description: What the request was for. Treated as `turn` when absent.

taskId.description: Your own id for the worker's task within the run.

attemptId.description: Your own id for this attempt at the task; retries get new ids.

parentSessionId.description: The `sessionId` of the session that spawned this one, for nested workers.

run.description: The completion run this call is made for. Its cost is claimed against that run's budget before the provider is called, and the call is refused with 422 `run_budget_exhausted` when it does not fit.

quest_master.description: Deprecated: the in-chat QuestMaster plan feature was removed. Always false.

id.description: Pass as `model` on the generation endpoints.

backend.description: The provider that serves the model.

blurb.description: How Studio introduces the model on its card: one line on what it is best at. Display text; may change. Set on catalog image models; null otherwise.

provider_label.description: The provider as shown to people (`OpenAI`, `Black Forest Labs`), where `backend` is the id. Display text. Set on catalog image models; null otherwise.

reasons_within_output_budget.description: Whether reasoning tokens are spent inside `max_output_tokens` on every turn. When true, a small `max_tokens` can be used up by reasoning alone and return an empty reply, so leave room above the answer you expect.

reasoning_efforts.description: The `reasoningEffort` levels this model acts on, lowest first; empty when it ignores the option. `none` is listed only where it turns reasoning off. Each level is mapped to the nearest one the provider offers. A listed level can still be dropped on one request: some OpenAI models drop it on tool turns, and Claude models with a fixed thinking budget drop it when `max_tokens` leaves no room for the budget plus the answer.

supports_tool_search.description: Whether the model accepts the tool search server tool and `defer_loading: true` on tool definitions, so a large tool catalog is searched on demand instead of loaded into context up front. Describes the model: `/api/ai/v1/completions` honours it for every model with this flag set, whether its `backend` is `anthropic` or `bedrock`.

supports_tool_changes.description: Whether a system-role message can carry `tool_addition` and `tool_removal` blocks, which add or remove a declared tool mid-conversation. Describes the model: `/api/ai/v1/completions` honours it only for models whose `backend` is `anthropic`; a `bedrock` model with this flag set is refused there with `errorCode: "tool_changes_unsupported"`.

supports_assistant_prefill.description: Whether `/api/ai/v1/completions` accepts a final assistant message for the model to continue. When false, a text prefill returns `400` with `errorCode: "assistant_prefill_unsupported"`; server-tool continuations are allowed. On Claude models that accept assistant prefill, it cannot be combined with `thinking`.

deprecation_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when no retirement is scheduled.

replaced_by.description: The id of the recommended successor, when there is one.

presets.description: Suggested `size` values; any `WxH` meeting `constraints` is accepted.

auto_size.description: The `size` value that lets the provider choose.

edge_multiple.description: Both edges must be a multiple of this.

max_aspect_ratio.description: Longest edge divided by shortest edge.

step.description: `width` and `height` are rounded to the nearest multiple of this.

kind.description: Takes an `aspect_ratio` such as `16:9`, not a `size`.
Sized by the input image; takes no `size`.
The provider takes no size at all.

qualities.description: Accepted `quality` tiers; empty when none is taken.

max_images.description: Most images one request may ask for via `n`.

max_reference_images.description: Most `referenceImageFabFileIds` honoured on generation; 0 when the model takes none. FLUX.2 edits take one fewer, as the source uses a slot.

image.description: Size rules and supported parameters. Present on image models only; null for every other type.

cached_input.description: Credits per 1M input tokens served from the provider prompt cache. Null where cached tokens are not billed separately, so they cost the `input` rate.

credits_per_1m_tokens.description: What a call is billed, in credits per 1M tokens, at the base context tier. Use it to compare models by cost. Null on non-text models and on any model with no published price; never 0 for an unpriced model.

id.description: Pass as `model` on the generation endpoints.

backend.description: The provider that serves the model.

blurb.description: How Studio introduces the model on its card: one line on what it is best at. Display text; may change. Set on catalog image models; null otherwise.

provider_label.description: The provider as shown to people (`OpenAI`, `Black Forest Labs`), where `backend` is the id. Display text. Set on catalog image models; null otherwise.

reasons_within_output_budget.description: Whether reasoning tokens are spent inside `max_output_tokens` on every turn. When true, a small `max_tokens` can be used up by reasoning alone and return an empty reply, so leave room above the answer you expect.

reasoning_efforts.description: The `reasoningEffort` levels this model acts on, lowest first; empty when it ignores the option. `none` is listed only where it turns reasoning off. Each level is mapped to the nearest one the provider offers. A listed level can still be dropped on one request: some OpenAI models drop it on tool turns, and Claude models with a fixed thinking budget drop it when `max_tokens` leaves no room for the budget plus the answer.

supports_tool_search.description: Whether the model accepts the tool search server tool and `defer_loading: true` on tool definitions, so a large tool catalog is searched on demand instead of loaded into context up front. Describes the model: `/api/ai/v1/completions` honours it for every model with this flag set, whether its `backend` is `anthropic` or `bedrock`.

supports_tool_changes.description: Whether a system-role message can carry `tool_addition` and `tool_removal` blocks, which add or remove a declared tool mid-conversation. Describes the model: `/api/ai/v1/completions` honours it only for models whose `backend` is `anthropic`; a `bedrock` model with this flag set is refused there with `errorCode: "tool_changes_unsupported"`.

supports_assistant_prefill.description: Whether `/api/ai/v1/completions` accepts a final assistant message for the model to continue. When false, a text prefill returns `400` with `errorCode: "assistant_prefill_unsupported"`; server-tool continuations are allowed. On Claude models that accept assistant prefill, it cannot be combined with `thinking`.

deprecation_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`; null when no retirement is scheduled.

replaced_by.description: The id of the recommended successor, when there is one.

presets.description: Suggested `size` values; any `WxH` meeting `constraints` is accepted.

auto_size.description: The `size` value that lets the provider choose.

edge_multiple.description: Both edges must be a multiple of this.

max_aspect_ratio.description: Longest edge divided by shortest edge.

step.description: `width` and `height` are rounded to the nearest multiple of this.

kind.description: Takes an `aspect_ratio` such as `16:9`, not a `size`.
Sized by the input image; takes no `size`.
The provider takes no size at all.

qualities.description: Accepted `quality` tiers; empty when none is taken.

max_images.description: Most images one request may ask for via `n`.

max_reference_images.description: Most `referenceImageFabFileIds` honoured on generation; 0 when the model takes none. FLUX.2 edits take one fewer, as the source uses a slot.

image.description: Size rules and supported parameters. Present on image models only; null for every other type.

cached_input.description: Credits per 1M input tokens served from the provider prompt cache. Null where cached tokens are not billed separately, so they cost the `input` rate.

credits_per_1m_tokens.description: What a call is billed, in credits per 1M tokens, at the base context tier. Use it to compare models by cost. Null on non-text models and on any model with no published price; never 0 for an unpriced model.

callbackUrl.description: Optional https URL that receives one signed POST when the job settles (success or failure). Requires API-key authentication and a callback signing secret on that key. The body is the GET /api/v1/quests/{id} response. Verify it with the `X-Webhook-Signature-256` header: `sha256=` + hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<X-Webhook-Timestamp>.<raw body>` keyed with the signing secret. Polling keeps working either way.

prompt_resolution.description: How the prompt is treated before it reaches the image model. `"auto"` (the default) resolves it against the session history, so a follow-up such as "make it darker" is rewritten to carry the previous subject and the prior image is fed back as input. `"literal"` skips that step: the prompt is sent unchanged (apart from truncation to the model's prompt limit), `intent` is `"fresh"`, `promptWasEnhanced` is `false`, and a prior session image is carried forward only for models that cannot run without an input image. Use `"literal"` when the prompt is already self-contained, for example when an agent or pipeline builds it.

post.description: Sends a message to the AI and creates a quest to process it. By default (async) the call returns immediately with a quest id; poll `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` for the reply. Send `wait: true` to block until the reply is ready and receive it inline. A `wait: true` turn is bounded at about 45 seconds: one that runs longer is ended (unused credits refunded) and answered with a 504 naming the quest in `quest_id`; one whose reasoning model spends its whole output budget thinking is answered with a 422 or 502 (see those responses). Send long or tool-heavy turns (large attachments, tool calls) in the default async mode and poll instead. A tool that produced machine-readable state reports it under `toolPayloads` - an array of `{ type, payload }` entries in emission order, alongside (never instead of) the prose reply - on the `wait: true` body and on the polled quest. A turn can FAIL after the ACK - reported on the polled quest as `type: "error"`, since the ACK was already sent. A terminal `status: "stopped"` (a missing session, a user-cancelled turn) is ALSO a failure even without `type: "error"` - it carries an explanatory string in `reply`/`replies` rather than an answer. `type` is the failure signal for the classified failure classes (an abort, a provider timeout, credit exhaustion); `errorCode` is an optional refinement present only when the failure has a classified reason. A recovered stuck quest is NOT in that list: one that still has renderable content resolves as a success by design. `QUEST_ERROR_CODES` has five members: `insufficient_credits`, `spend_cap_exceeded`, `spend_frozen`, `free_quest_limit_reached`, and `run_budget_exhausted`. `insufficient_credits` and `spend_frozen` are raised as quest errorCodes on this endpoint: a spending pause in force when the request arrives is refused synchronously with a 403, and one that lands after the ACK reaches the quest. `free_quest_limit_reached` is no longer raised: it survives only on quests that settled with it before the in-chat QuestMaster plan was retired. `spend_cap_exceeded` is thrown only by the embed chat route's pre-flight, which fires outside the process try/catch that would classify it onto a quest, and `run_budget_exhausted` only by image generation. A turn that prompt moderation refuses settles as `type: "error"` with `errorCode: "content_blocked"` and the refusal text in `reply`, on the 200 `wait: true` body and on the polled quest alike; do not resend it unchanged. A caller must treat `type: "error"` OR a terminal `status: "stopped"` as failure even when `errorCode` is absent, and must not read `reply` as an answer without checking those first. Organization-policy preflight refusals use 403 with `errorCode: "org_model_not_allowed"` or `"org_tool_not_allowed"`. An explicit-model JWT request can instead be accepted and refused during quest execution: that refusal appears on the 200 `wait: true` body or polled quest as `type: "error"`, without a policy `errorCode`. Check the quest outcome as described above. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) or a JWT. Session resolution: pass `sessionId` to continue an existing notebook. An API-key caller that omits it gets a BRAND-NEW notebook rather than the notebook the human last had open, and `newConversation: true` forces a new notebook for any auth mode; both return the new id as `sessionId`, so the caller can continue the conversation by passing it back. A first-party JWT caller that omits `sessionId` keeps the last-opened-notebook fallback. Sending `sessionId` and `newConversation` together is a 422.

200.description: Message accepted - NOT a completed turn. The default (async) path returns this queued ACK; the outcome arrives on `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` (see the `sendChatMessage200PollResult` schema). With `wait: true` the body is instead the completed turn: the ACK fields plus the reply (`response`/`responses`), `toolPayloads`, `createdAt`, `performance` timings and, when requested, `promptDetails`/`promptText`. A turn that FAILS still resolves with `200`, never a 4xx, on both that `wait: true` body and the polled quest (`GET /api/v1/quests/{id}`) - the prose explaining why lands in `reply`/`response` like any other answer, so the reply text alone cannot tell a failure from an answer. `type` is the field that can: both surfaces carry it unconditionally, so match on `type: "error"` first - it covers credit exhaustion, a provider timeout or overload, and an in-process aborted turn; a real answer carries the turn's actual completion type instead (`"message"` for an ordinary reply). Two related states do NOT set `type: "error"`: a user-cancelled turn resolves as `status: "stopped"` with `type` left at `"message"`, and a recovered stuck quest that still has renderable content resolves as a success (`status: "done"`, no error) by design, to avoid destroying content to report a failure. The one exception is output-budget exhaustion: a `wait: true` request answers it with the 422 or 502 error envelope (plus `quest_id`) instead of this body. `errorCode` names a classified failure: `insufficient_credits` or `spend_frozen` (a spending pause that landed after the ACK). Other `type: "error"` turns may have no classifier, so never use its absence to infer success. On a real answer `errorCode` is absent from the `wait: true` body. The body also carries `sessionId`, the notebook the turn was recorded in - for an API-key caller that sent none (or any caller sending `newConversation: true`), that is the freshly created notebook's id; pass it back as the request's `sessionId` to continue. Contrast the tts/music/soundEffects contracts, which reject synchronously with a 422 carrying the same `errorCode` vocabulary.

post.description: Runs the tool-using agent (ReAct) loop against a session - the same pipeline the product UI's Agent Mode toggle dispatches to, and the REST equivalent of the `agent_execute` WebSocket command. The run is asynchronous: this returns `202` with an execution id, and the caller polls `GET /api/v1/agent-executions/{id}` until `status` is terminal (`completed`, `failed`, or `aborted`). Nothing is streamed back over REST - for live iteration events, use the WebSocket route instead. Omit `agent_id` to get the profile the session's own surface resolves to, which is what reproduces the in-app toggle. The final reply is also written to the session as a normal chat message, so it appears in history. Naming a tool in `tools` also PRE-APPROVES it for the run: there is no interactive client to answer a permission prompt, so a run that calls an approval-gated tool you did not name fails with that tool named in `error` rather than hanging. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) or a JWT.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible completion. A successful request is ALWAYS answered with an SSE stream (`text/event-stream`), regardless of the `stream` flag: a `meta` event, then `content`/`tool_use` events carrying `usage`/`credits`, then one `settled` event once credits are committed (the charge can be 0), terminated by `data: [DONE]`. The terminal event carries `stopReason`; treat `max_tokens` as a TRUNCATED reply rather than a complete one, and note that omitting `max_tokens` on the request lets the server size the output ceiling for the model (recommended for reasoning models, which spend thinking tokens inside that ceiling). A message `content` may be a string or an array of parts; image parts are accepted in OpenAI Chat (`image_url`), OpenAI Responses (`input_image`) or Anthropic (`image` with a `source`) form and are translated to whatever the target model speaks. A final non-blank assistant message is an assistant prefill, except a server-tool continuation ending in `server_tool_use` or `tool_search_tool_result`. Plain system prompts and blank messages are ignored. Check the model's `supports_assistant_prefill` field from `GET /api/v1/models` before sending one. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) or a JWT.

END USERS. A key that serves many end users of your own product, and that an administrator has granted `ai:end-user-id`, may send `end_user_id` (your opaque id for the end user) so that, on models served directly by OpenAI or Anthropic, the model provider sees each end user separately rather than your whole account as one (other providers receive no end-user identifier).

RUNS AND SETTLEMENT. To group the spend of a multi-agent run (a root session and the workers it spawns), mint a run id with `POST /api/v1/completion-runs` and send it as `run` on each request. Spend is recorded against the run, never charged twice. The `settled` event (`{ type, requestId, creditsCharged, usdCost, runId }`) arrives after the last content event and before `[DONE]`, once the charge is committed: `creditsCharged` is what the ledger recorded, which can be below the terminal event's `credits.used` when the balance capped it, and `requestId` is the `X-Request-ID` you sent (or a generated one). Use it to count a settled charge once when your client sees the same event twice (replay or reconnect). Send a fresh `X-Request-ID` per request: reusing one does not deduplicate charges, since the server charges every request.

TOOL SEARCH. On a model whose `GET /api/v1/models` row has `supports_tool_search: true` (`backend` `"anthropic"` or `"bedrock"`), a `tools` entry may set `toolSchema.defer_loading: true`, and a `{ "serverTool": { "type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex" } }` (or the `bm25` pair) entry adds Anthropic's tool search, so deferred definitions load only when the model searches for them. The stream then carries `provider_block` events (`{ type, provider: "anthropic", block }`) for the server-run search; echo each block back verbatim, in order, in the assistant `messages` content of the next request, and never answer one with a `tool_result`. When the server-run search loop hits its iteration limit the stream ends with `stopReason: "pause_turn"`; continue by re-sending the conversation with that assistant turn's provider blocks echoed. A client-side search may return `{ "type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "..." }` blocks inside a `tool_result`'s content. On every other model `defer_loading` is ignored (every tool is sent as usual) and a server tool, a `tool_reference` or an echoed tool search block is refused with a `400` rather than run without it.

ERRORS. Everything checked before the model provider is called fails with a JSON error body and a real HTTP status, before any stream opens: an empty `messages` array, a conversation with no non-empty user or assistant message (system-only, or only blank content), a malformed request, or an unknown `model` `400` (`errorCode: "unknown_model"` for an unknown model), a bad credential `401`, a key without a required scope `403` (with `required_scopes`), a free-tier account calling a model outside the free-tier allowlist `403` with `errorCode: "model_requires_subscription"` (upgrade the plan or pick a free-tier model), a model the caller's organization policy does not allow `403` with `errorCode: "org_model_not_allowed"`, paused spending `403` with `errorCode: "spend_frozen"`, a body over 25 MB `413`, any other body that fails schema validation `422`, insufficient credits `422` with `errorCode: "insufficient_credits"` (personal or org balance, or an org per-member credit cap), a `run` minted with a budget that has too little left for even a short answer `422` with `errorCode: "run_budget_exhausted"` (retry once in-flight requests on the run settle, or raise the run budget; buying credits does not), a rate limit `429` with `Retry-After`, a `run` that does not exist or that another user or billing owner minted `404` with `errorCode: "run_not_found"`, and a catalogued model whose provider is not configured on this deployment, or a model that could only come from a self-hosted model server (Ollama, local image) that is currently unreachable, `503` with `errorCode: "provider_not_configured"` (retryable). A provider rejection of caller input that happens before the stream opens is also a JSON `400`, with `errorCode: "invalid_request"` (do not retry it unchanged). Once the stream has opened the status stays `200` and a failure arrives as one terminal in-band `error` event. Branch on that event's `code`, never on `message`, which is prose and may change: `insufficient_credits` (buy credits) when credits run out mid-generation, `invalid_request` when the provider rejects caller input (do not retry it unchanged), `provider_rejected` when the model provider refused our credentials, `content_blocked` when the model declined the request (do not retry it unchanged), `output_budget_exhausted` when a reasoning model spent your whole `max_tokens` thinking and wrote no answer (raise `max_tokens` or omit it; do not retry it unchanged), and `provider_error` for any other provider failure. Treat `code` as optional.

post.description:
Adds a user message to an existing session (called a "notebook" in the product UI) and runs the assistant reply through the same pipeline as the web app, so the turn appears in the session and every other client watching it sees it live. A successful request is answered with an SSE stream (`text/event-stream`): a `meta` event carrying `requestId`, a `turn` event with the new `quest_id` and `session_id`, then `delta` events (`{ quest_id, slot, text }`) that each APPEND `text` to reply slot `slot`, and `replace` events (`{ quest_id, slot, text }`) that REPLACE a slot whole when the server reset or rewrote it (a retry, a rapid-reply handoff). Thinking models stream their reasoning in an earlier slot than the answer. One `settled` event (`{ quest_id, status, failed, credits_used, error_code }`) follows the last slot event, then `data: [DONE]`. `status` is `done` or `stopped`; when `failed` is true the slots hold an explanation rather than an answer, and `error_code` names the cause when it is a known one.

DISCONNECTS. Closing the stream detaches from the turn; it does not stop it. The turn runs to the end and is saved to the session, and an API key's concurrent-request slot stays held until the turn finishes. Stop a turn with `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stop-reply`.

ERRORS. Everything checked before the turn starts fails with a JSON error body and a real HTTP status, before any stream opens: a bad credential `401`; a key without `ai:chat` `403` (with `required_scopes`); a suspended account, paused spending or an organization the caller cannot bill `403` with an `errorCode`; a `model` that does not exist, is disabled or cannot run a chat completion `400`; a `session_id` that does not exist or that the caller cannot write to `404` (the two are indistinguishable on purpose); a body that fails schema validation `422`; too many requests, or the free-tier daily allowance used up, `429` with `Retry-After`. Once the turn exists the stream opens and the status stays `200`: a turn the account cannot pay for (`error_code: "insufficient_credits"`) or a model its plan or organization does not allow is reported by its `settled` event with `failed: true`, like any other failed turn, and an `error` event is sent only when the server could not follow the turn to its end.

post.description:
Mints a run id that groups the spend of several `POST /api/ai/v1/completions` requests, such as a root session and the workers it spawns. Send the returned `runId` as `run.runId` on each of those requests. The run is bound to the credential that minted it: the same user and the same billing owner (the organization for an organization-billed API key or the `organization_id` sent, otherwise the user), and a completion naming a run minted by anyone else is refused with `404` (`errorCode: "run_not_found"`). Minting a run charges nothing, and attributing a completion to it never charges that completion twice.

With `budgetCredits`, the run also caps admission: what its completions may claim together. Before calling the model, each completion claims what its first round can cost at its full output budget (less, down to what a short answer costs, when the run has less left) and is capped to that claim, so concurrent completions can never together be admitted past the budget. The claim is priced from an estimate of the input, so a completion that costs more than it claimed is still charged its actual cost, up to what the balance can pay; the run counts that cost and refuses later claims it can no longer cover. A run can go over its budget by at most that miss for each completion in flight. A completion that runs server-side tools claims more the same way before each further round, and ends with `stopReason: "max_tokens"` when the run cannot cover one. A completion the budget cannot cover is refused with `422` (`errorCode: "run_budget_exhausted"`) before anything is charged. Claims return to the run when their completion settles, fails or is abandoned. The account balance and any organization member caps still apply on their own, and buying credits does not raise a run budget. The budget bounds charged credits, so a deployment that does not charge for completions counts nothing against it.

201.description: The created run, or the existing evaluation for the same owner and rootSessionId. Evaluation mint retries preserve the original immutable limits and receipts.

post.description: Generates speech from text using OpenAI or ElevenLabs. When the requested provider has no usable key (or the provider rejects it), another configured provider stands in and the substitution is reported via `provider`/`fallbackFrom` and the `X-B4M-Tts-Provider*` headers. Input length is capped per provider (OpenAI 4096 characters, ElevenLabs 10000), and an output `format` the chosen provider cannot produce is rejected with a 422 before any provider cost is incurred. `organization_id` picks the payer: an organization you belong to, or null for your personal credits; omitted bills your personal credits, as this endpoint always has. The default `encoding: "binary"` returns the raw audio bytes; `encoding: "base64"` returns JSON. Audio over the ~4MB response ceiling is returned by signed URL (a `303` for binary, the `delivery: "url"` variant for base64). Generated audio is saved to the file browser unless the call sets `preview`; the outcome is reported in the JSON save fields and the `X-B4M-Audio-*` headers - fetch the saved copy from `fileUrl` / `X-B4M-Audio-File-Url`, since `GET /api/files/{id}` fails closed until moderation completes. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) or a JWT.

200.description: Speech synthesized. Binary bodies carry a Content-Type that follows the requested `format` (`audio/mpeg` for mp3, else `audio/wav`, `audio/opus`, `audio/aac`, `audio/flac`, `audio/pcm`). The default `encoding: "binary"` returns the raw audio bytes; `encoding: "base64"` returns the JSON body. Audio over the ~4MB response ceiling cannot ride in the body: the binary encoding answers `303` instead, and the base64 encoding returns the `delivery: "url"` variant, whose `url` is a time-limited signed GET for the audio (`bytes` is its size).

get.description: Returns the authenticated caller: stable id, display name, plan tier, personal credit balance, and entitlement keys. The subject is always the credential holder - this endpoint accepts no user id, owner id, or impersonation parameter of any kind, so a key can only ever read its own owner. `credits.balance` is the caller's personal ledger; a call billed to an organization draws on a pool this number does not describe. `credits.monthly_allowance` totals monthly personal plan grants, including custom grants; it is null when unavailable and may be omitted by older servers. `credits.expiring` lists the part of the personal balance due to expire, soonest first. Each `amount` is what remains of that grant once the balance has fallen below the grants' total: credits no entry covers are spent first and do not expire. It may be omitted by older servers. Gate on `tier != "free"` for "does this caller hold a paid plan (own or org seat)" and on `subscription.price_id` for which product - the `basic`/`pro` rungs come from an internal plan ladder and do not track a plan's marketing name. An org seat (a Team plan held by the caller's organization) confers that org plan's tier and `subscription`, even when the caller pays nothing personally, so `tier != "free"` does not by itself mean the caller is billed. Responses are never cacheable. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) carrying `me:read`, or a JWT.

**Deprecated, sunset 2027-02-17.** Use `/api/v1/image-jobs` instead. Queues an image generation and returns immediately with the quest that will carry the result - no image yet, and the call never blocks on the render. Poll `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` until `status` is `"done"` (see the `generateImage200PollResult` schema). Omit `sessionId` to create a new session. The prompt is resolved against the session history first, so a follow-up such as "make it darker" binds to the previous image; `enhancedPrompt` reports the prompt actually sent to the model. Send `prompt_resolution: "literal"` to skip that step and have the prompt sent as written (apart from truncation to the model's prompt limit). `referenceImageFabFileIds` passes up to 15 already-uploaded images as style anchors, after the input image taken from `fabFileIds`. GPT-image accepts 15 references; FLUX.2 accepts 8 total input images (4 for Klein) and FLUX 3 accepts 10. For FLUX.2 and FLUX 3 the distinct ids across `fabFileIds` and `referenceImageFabFileIds` are counted together when `referenceImageFabFileIds` is set, and a request over the limit is rejected with a 400. A request over the limit with only `fabFileIds`, or with a primary picked from session history, is checked when the render runs and fails on the polled quest. Unsupported models are also rejected with a 400. FLUX 3 receives its inputs as `ref_image_1` to `ref_image_N`, in this order: the first `fabFileIds` image (so `ref_image_1` when one is attached), the remaining `fabFileIds` images, then `referenceImageFabFileIds` as listed. A repeated id, or an image with identical content, keeps only its first position, which shifts the later tags. Refer to them in the prompt, e.g. "the jacket from ref_image_2". Which `size` values a model accepts, and whether it honours `background`, `seed`, `quality`, `n` and reference images, is listed per model in the `image` block of `GET /api/v1/models`. Credits are checked when the render runs, so insufficient credits arrive on the polled quest rather than as a 422. A `run` budget is checked before queueing as well, so a run with too little left is usually a synchronous 422 (`errorCode: "run_budget_exhausted"`). `organization_id` is accepted as an alias of `organizationId`, for callers used to the snake_case video and music bodies; `null` bills the personal account. `POST /api/ai/generate-image` is a legacy alias of this endpoint. The body is the `GET /api/v1/quests/{id}` response. post.summary: Start an image generation or edit
post.description: Queues `count` images (default 1), one job each, and returns `202` with the jobs and their shared `group_id`. Poll `GET /api/v1/image-jobs/{id}` for each job until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`. `mode: "generate"` renders from the prompt; `mode: "edit"` changes the `edit_source` input, optionally within a `mask` or `edit_regions`. Input images are files you uploaded (`POST /api/v1/files`). The prompt is sent as written. Check the request against the model in `GET /api/v1/image-models`: an unsupported size, aspect ratio, quality, input or option is a 422 naming it, never silently adjusted. A finished image is saved to your Files with the `generated` tag (if that save fails it is kept outside Files and `output.file_id` is null). On success, `output.availability` says whether it can be downloaded: `ready` means `output.url` is a signed download URL valid for 15 minutes (re-fetch the job for a fresh one); `pending_scan` means the saved file is still being scanned, so keep re-fetching the job; `unavailable` means the file was blocked or deleted, so stop polling. Credits for the model's price are reserved up front per image and settled on completion; a failed or cancelled job is not charged. A `blocked` job is not charged either, unless the provider rendered the image before it was rejected and billed it: then `credits.settled` shows the charge. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-255 printable ASCII characters) to make retries safe: a repeat with the same key and body returns the original jobs, and the same key with a different body is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to the billed account and to `count`, so the same key sent with a different `count` or `organization_id` starts new jobs, which are charged. Set `organization_id` to bill an organization you belong to, or `null` to bill your personal credits; omitted, the jobs bill your home organization (or your personal credits if you have none). An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization (see `organization_id`). This replaces `POST /api/v1/image-generations` and `POST /api/v1/image-edits`.

post.description: Returns one embedding vector per input string. The request and success bodies follow the OpenAI embeddings API shape; error bodies use the standard B4M error envelope. `model` is any embedding model returned by GET /api/v1/embedding-models; `input` is a string or up to 2048 strings, at most 300000 tokens in total and each within the model context window. The input count is further capped so inputs x output width stays within 196608 values (128 inputs at 1536 dimensions) - page larger jobs across requests. Pre-tokenized input (arrays of token ids) is not accepted; clients that send it by default, such as LangChain's Python `OpenAIEmbeddings`, must be set to send strings (`check_embedding_ctx_length=False`). `dimensions` shortens the vector on models that support it (OpenAI `text-embedding-3-*`, and Voyage models with several published widths). Optional `input_type` is `query` or `document`; providers without task hints ignore it. Billed in credits per input token from the per-model embedding rate, reserved before the provider call and refunded if it fails. post.description: Evaluates each question independently against the same `input` and returns calibrated probabilities - no generated text. Question types: `predicate` (probability a statement is true), `choice` (pick one value) and `score` (an ordered scale; `score` is the probability-weighted mean of 0-based level indices). `confidence` is computed by B4M with one published formula for every model. Answers come back in question order; a question the model declines is a `refusal` answer and does not fail the request. `input` is a string or a list of `text`, `json` and `image` parts; an image is a `file_id` you can read or a base64 `data:` URL (http(s) URLs are rejected). Platform ceilings: 50 questions, 64 choices, 2-10 levels and 8 images; each model's own caps are listed by `GET /api/v1/decision-models` and a request over one is a 422 naming the cap and `param`. Probabilities are not comparable across models: tune thresholds per model against labelled examples, and pin a versioned model id when you do. A busy provider is retried once on the same model, never another; after that the response is a 503 with `Retry-After`. Billed per input and output token at the model's rate, settled to the exact expected cost (most calls charge 0 credits, some 1). Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) carrying `ai:decide` or `ai:generate`, or a JWT.

post.description: Finds the sessions of yours whose conversations match a query. By default it first keeps the messages that contain the query terms (after spelling correction and synonym expansion), then ranks them by embedding similarity, so a result is both on topic and close in meaning. Messages without a stored embedding are embedded on the fly up to a cap; `partial` says the cap was hit. The query expansion, embeddings and re-rank run on platform keys and are billed in credits to the caller, reserved before each call and refunded if it fails. get.description: Returns a lake member's ingestion status. Adding a file to a lake does NOT ingest it: a file only becomes searchable once it has been chunked and embedded, so poll this endpoint until `ingestion_status` is `ready`. `indexing` clears on its own; `paused` means re-processing was stopped partway and needs the file reprocessed (or background lake work resumed) before it returns; `failed` carries the reason in `error`. A `ready` file can also carry a non-null `error` when a later pass failed partway: its committed passages stay searchable, so branch on `ingestion_status`, not on `error`. `not_ingested` means the file has no searchable passages yet: ingestion has not started, a first pass has not committed its chunks, or the file has no extractable text (such a file never becomes `ready`). These agree with what search reports under `retrieval_unavailable`.

post.description: Queues a video generation and returns `202` with the job. Poll `GET /api/v1/video-generations/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`. On success, `output.availability` says whether the clip can be downloaded: `ready` means `output.url` is a signed download URL valid for 15 minutes (re-fetch the job for a fresh one); `pending_scan` means the saved file is still being scanned, so keep re-fetching the job (self-hosted installs can stay here for up to ~30 minutes); `unavailable` means the file was blocked or deleted and `output.url` will never be set, so stop polling. Credits for the requested duration are reserved up front and settled on completion; a failed or cancelled job is not charged. A `blocked` job is not charged either, unless the provider generated the clip before rejecting it and billed it: then the requested duration is charged and `credits.settled` shows it. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-255 printable ASCII characters) to make retries safe: a repeat with the same key and body returns the original job, and the same key with a different body is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Omitted fields take the model defaults from `GET /api/v1/video-models`. Set `organization_id` to bill an organization you belong to, or `null` to bill your personal credits; omitted, the job bills your home organization (or your personal credits if you have none). Keys are scoped to the billed account, so the same key sent for a different `organization_id` starts a new job. An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization (see `organization_id`).

202.description: Accepted; the job is queued (or replayed for a repeated Idempotency-Key).

post.description: Queues a song and returns `202` with the job. Poll `GET /api/v1/music-generations/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled`. A finished song is saved to your Files with the `generated` tag (if that save fails it is kept outside Files and `output.file_id` is null). On success, `output.availability` says whether it can be downloaded: `ready` means `output.url` is a signed download URL valid for 15 minutes (re-fetch the job for a fresh one); `pending_scan` means the saved file is still being scanned, so keep re-fetching the job (self-hosted installs can stay here for up to ~30 minutes); `unavailable` means the file was blocked or deleted and `output.url` will never be set, so stop polling. Credits for the model's price are reserved up front and settled on completion; a failed or cancelled job is not charged. A `blocked` job is not charged either, unless the provider generated the song before rejecting it and billed it: then the price is charged and `credits.settled` shows it. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-255 printable ASCII characters) to make retries safe: a repeat with the same key and body returns the original job, and the same key with a different body is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Omitted fields take the model defaults from `GET /api/v1/music-models`. Set `organization_id` to bill an organization you belong to, or `null` to bill your personal credits; omitted, the job bills your home organization (or your personal credits if you have none). Keys are scoped to the billed account, so the same key sent for a different `organization_id` starts a new job. An organization-billed API key always bills its own organization (see `organization_id`).

post.summary: Compose a Scene from a video and a music track
post.description: Queues a Scene: one shareable clip made from a video file and an audio file you own, with optional cover art, and returns `202` with the job. The Scene runs exactly as long as the video: its picture is copied unchanged and the audio is trimmed (or looped) to fit, with optional fades. The video may run at most 300 seconds, and the input files together may total at most 200 MB. A Scene over your Files per-file size limit is still rendered, but is stored outside Files: its output has a null file_id and a files_skip_reason. Poll `GET /api/v1/scene-compositions/{id}` until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`. The finished Scene is saved to your Files with the `generated` and `scene` tags, linked to its inputs (see `GET /api/v1/files/{id}/lineage`); if that save fails it is kept outside Files and `output.file_id` is null. `output.availability` works as on the other generation jobs: `ready` means `output.url` is a signed download URL valid for 15 minutes (re-fetch the job for a fresh one), `pending_scan` means keep re-fetching, and `unavailable` means stop polling. A file that cannot be read as the media its slot needs (no video stream, an over-long video) ends the job `failed` with `unsupported_input`. Composing is free: no credits are reserved or charged. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-255 printable ASCII characters) to make retries safe: a repeat with the same key and body returns the original job, and the same key with a different body is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.

post.description:
Transcribes an upload minted by `POST /api/v1/transcriptions/uploads` and returns the text. Call it within 5 minutes of minting the upload. Credits are charged by file size. The uploaded audio is deleted when the call returns, whether it succeeds or fails, so each upload can be transcribed once.

**Limit:** this call is synchronous. Provider work stops being awaited after 45 seconds from request arrival, leaving time to return reserved credits and delete the upload before the hosted server stops at 60 seconds. A slow recording returns a gateway timeout (`504`) instead of text. AWS batch jobs cannot be cancelled remotely and may finish later; their output expires automatically. Do not retry with the same `file_key`: mint a new upload and send shorter audio. If cleanup fails, the upload may not be deleted right away (it expires on its own).

post.description: Posts a message to a Slack channel, or a reply in a thread with `thread_ts`, as the Bike4Mind bot. Returns the message `ts`; pass it back as `thread_ts` to reply in that thread. Three things must hold: the key carries `slack:post`; the channel is in a Slack workspace connected to an organization the key's owner belongs to (an organization-billed key must bill that same organization); and an owner of that same organization (or a platform admin) has enabled the channel for API posting, optionally limited to listed key ids. Disconnecting the workspace turns every opt-in off. `slack:post` is a confined scope: a posting key carries no other scope and reaches no other route. Mint one from the organization's Slack integration settings. The bot must also be a member of the channel: invite it with `/invite @<bot name>`. `text` is at most 3000 characters and is the notification fallback when `blocks` (Block Kit, at most 49 blocks and 40000 serialized characters) is sent. Blocks are limited to section, header, divider, context, image, rich_text; nothing a reader can act on is accepted: no interactive elements, `action_id`, `confirm`, or `url` outside a rich_text link, and a section `accessory` must be an image. Broadcast mentions (`<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`, user groups, and bare `@channel` / `@here` / `@everyone`) are posted as plain text that notifies nobody; `<@U...>` user mentions are kept. Every post ends with a context block naming the posting user and key, and carries message metadata marking it as an API post; Slack actions on it are ignored. A block Slack rejects as malformed answers 422. Rate limited to 30 messages a minute and 1,000 a day per key and per user, and 60 a minute per channel, on top of the key's own limits. Authenticate with an API key (`b4m_live_`) carrying `slack:post`.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: Chat, completions, embeddings, and server-side tool execution.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Sessions (called "notebooks" in the product UI) and their attached knowledge.

tags.name: Release notes
tags.description: Customer-facing notes on what changed in each release. Public.

tags.name: Audio
tags.description: Speech, music, and sound-effect generation. For music, use `POST /api/v1/music-generations`; `/api/ai/music` is deprecated.

tags.name: Music
tags.description: Song generation, queued with `202` and polled at `GET /api/v1/music-generations/{id}`.

tags.name: Scenes
tags.description: A video and a music track composed into one shareable clip, queued with `202` and polled at `GET /api/v1/scene-compositions/{id}`.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Image generation and editing, queued with `202` and polled at `GET /api/v1/image-jobs/{id}`. `/api/v1/image-generations` and `/api/v1/image-edits` are deprecated.

tags.name: Transcriptions
tags.description: Speech-to-text: upload an audio file, then transcribe it.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Diagrams, charts, code and documents kept in sessions, with their version history.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Upload files and fetch any file by id, with short-lived signed download URLs.

tags.name: Videos
tags.description: Video generation, queued with `202` and polled at `GET /api/v1/video-generations/{id}`.

tags.name: Voice
tags.description: Real-time voice conversations: list voices, open a call, and reconcile its credits when it ends.

tags.name: Models
tags.description: The models the caller can use, and the parameters each one accepts.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The caller's own identity, plan tier, credit balance, and entitlements.

tags.name: Data Lakes
tags.description: Curated document collections: list and inspect the lakes you can reach, manage which files belong to one, check each file's ingestion status, and run semantic search over a single lake.

tags.name: Data Lake Research
tags.description: Saved research configs, on-demand and scheduled runs, the proposal review queue they fill, and the lake's configuration history. Reading and changing these needs manage rights on the lake.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Workspaces that group sessions and files: list and read the projects you can reach, and create new ones.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Custom agents with their own system prompt, model settings and tool access: list, read and manage them.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Create, update and read your own skills from a SKILL.md, and the Skill Market: your organization's approved listings, served as a Claude Code plugin marketplace.

tags.name: Functions
tags.description: Your live functions: Python artifacts saved as functions and promoted after their tests passed on the server. List and read them, and call one to get its output with a stamp of what it ran on.

tags.name: Slack
tags.description: Post status messages and thread replies to Slack channels through the Bike4Mind bot, without holding a Slack token.

tags.name: Tools
tags.description: Built-in tools for your own agent loop: web search, reading a web page, and the current weather, each returned as text a model can read.
